comment: The email address goes in the ID token on purpose: applications (e.g. the first-party SaaS) read it there without a userinfo call. A 'should', not a 'must'.
The email address goes in the ID token on purpose: applications (e.g. the first-party SaaS) read it there without a userinfo call. A 'should', not a 'must'.
Only 'name' is kept for a person (no given/family name, picture, locale...): the profile scope returns what exists. A 'should'.
No authentication context classes are defined (amr tells password or password + one-time code). A 'should'.
